_comment: Scan-root liveness. Every COVERAGE-BEARING root a gate policy declares must resolve to a real path (or, for a glob, match at least one). A dead root means the gate scans less than it claims and reports GREEN over an empty set - and because the fleet's anti-narrowing ratchet forbids REMOVING a root, a reorg move that empties one leaves it permanently dead AND unremovable. Keys are the FULL JSON POINTER, not the leaf name: `roots` appears at three different nesting levels inside rust-first-automation-policy.json alone, so leaf-name keying would collapse distinct declarations and let one baselined entry silently tolerate another. Only coverage-bearing keys are in scope; vocabulary lists (exclude_prefixes, allowed_paths, forbidden_prefixes) are excluded because a dead entry there excludes or permits nothing. forward_declarations hold paths declared deliberately BEFORE they exist - flagging those would punish declaring a reorg destination ahead of the move - and a forward declaration whose path LANDS must be retired so it cannot become a permanent unaudited exemption. baselined_dead_roots is FROZEN and shrink-only.

_provenance.policy: shrink-only; a NEW dead root fails, and a landed forward declaration must be retired
_provenance._build_root_retired_2026_08_09: The three `::build` forward declarations (dto-authz-trust, embedded-asset-hermeticity, authz-coverage) were RETIRED here because build/ landed its first crate — build/port-engine/core/port-engine-kernel, PR #1621 — which is verbatim the event their own reason strings named (`Created when build/ lands its first crate`). Retirement is a DELETION FROM THIS EXEMPTION MAP ONLY: `build` stays in all three policies' scan_roots arrays untouched, and now resolves, so it is a live audited root rather than an unaudited standing exemption. That is the whole point of forward_declarations being pinned by forward_declarations_are_all_still_absent: a declaration whose path arrives must stop being tolerated in the same change that makes it real. Sibling roots base/ and policy/ remain absent and remain declared; whoever lands their first crate owes the same one-line retirement. app/ was later retired in _app_root_retired_2026_08_11. NOT retired here: module-membership declared no `build` entry, so it had nothing to retire.
_provenance._build_widening_measured_2026_08_09: The widening is not free of consequence and was measured rather than assumed. embedded-asset-hermeticity now walks build/, and the new crate carries four include_str! sites (src/lib.rs:78 `lib.rs`, src/lib.rs:93 `../tests/seams.rs`, tests/neutrality.rs:42 `../src/lib.rs`, tests/neutrality.rs:48 `seams.rs`). All four resolve inside targets whose BUCK srcs already provide them — the library globs `src/**/*.rs` plus `tests/seams.rs`, and the neutrality test globs all three — so the gate stays green with no baseline movement. caller-supplied-authorization and endpoint-authorization-coverage now walk build/ too; the kernel exposes no DTO deserialization and no HTTP endpoint, so both are likewise zero-delta. Verified by running all three gates, not by reading the policies.
_provenance._app_root_retired_2026_08_11: The four `::app` forward declarations (dto-authz-trust, embedded-asset-hermeticity, authz-coverage, module-membership) were RETIRED here because app/ landed its first tracked path — app/README.md on integ/app (PR #1668, OVERRULE 3d glue-only). Retirement is a DELETION FROM THIS EXEMPTION MAP ONLY: `app` stays in each policy's scan_roots arrays untouched, and now resolves, so it is a live audited root. README-only (zero crates) keeps hermeticity/authz widening zero-delta. Sibling roots base/ and policy/ remain absent and remain declared.
_provenance._cloud_root_retired_2026_08_17: The top-level cloud/ tree is intentionally retired, but its seven remaining coverage-bearing declarations stay in their owning policies so future reintroduction is scanned immediately and anti-narrowing cannot be bypassed as cleanup. Those exact fully qualified declarations move into the frozen shrink-only baseline; the live exact-set test binds the baseline to all and only currently dead non-forward roots.
_provenance._dark_gate_burndown_2026_08_19: Three governance/check crates left baselined_dark_gate_crates (100 -> 97) because each gained a live-corpus test that reads this tree and freezes its findings shrink-only and two-sided: authz-tier-discipline (tests/authz_tier_discipline_live.rs, 544 Cedar policies + 4 Envoy configs, 138 tier leaks over 60 (file, needle) keys, ADR-0191), event-schema-versioning (tests/event_schema_versioning.rs, 88 AsyncAPI documents, 73 unversioned, ADR-0154), idempotency-key-coverage (tests/idempotency_key_coverage.rs, 138 OpenAPI documents / 602 state-changing operations, 522 uncovered, ADR-0149). Censuses measured on dev @ 889027711, the commit that deleted 51 unreferenced product crates. Removal is required, not optional: CODE_STALE_DARK_GATE_BASELINE fires on a baselined crate that has since gained a live test, so the burn-down is recorded in the same change that earns it. None of the three is vacuous - every one names a non-empty subject and a non-zero finding set, and each carries a mutation test that injects the defect it exists to catch into REAL corpus text and asserts the kernel reddens.
_provenance._dark_gate_burndown_lane_c_2026_08_19: Two governance/check crates left baselined_dark_gate_crates (97 -> 95, after the three that PR #2164 connected) because each gained a live-corpus test that reads this tree and freezes its findings shrink-only and two-sided: cursor-pagination-coverage (tests/cursor_pagination_coverage.rs, 138 OpenAPI documents / 469 get operations, 60 collection-shaped gets with no cursor + page_size, ADR-0150) and data-class (tests/data_class_coverage.rs, 150 kernel-tier workspace members / 2762 pub struct fields, 733 unannotated of which 459 carry no ledger allowance, MFL-0008). Censuses measured on dev @ bc6e04fa1. Removal is required, not optional: CODE_STALE_DARK_GATE_BASELINE fires on a baselined crate that has since gained a live test, so the burn-down is recorded in the same change that earns it. Neither is vacuous - each names a non-empty subject and a non-zero finding set, and each carries a mutation test that injects the defect it exists to catch into REAL corpus text and asserts the kernel reddens. data-class also repaired its allowance ledger in the same change: every row in registry/data-class/legacy-unannotated-fields.tsv pointed at `crates/...`, a root that no longer exists because those 13 shared kernels MOVED to `libs/`, so the ledger had stopped matching a single live field.

ci/facade/caller-supplied-authorization/.reason: Same pre-widening as app/ above. base/ is the ADR-0562 shared floor (>=3 capability consumers); a primitive there can carry an authorization DTO, so the class-fix must see it from the moment it lands. Created by the first libs/ consolidation move.

Same pre-widening as app/ above. policy is the capability ADR-0615 extracted from iam and is where PBAC/PDP code lands — the single root where a caller-supplied-authz defect would be most consequential. Created when the policy capability lands its first crate.

ci/facade/embedded-asset-hermeticity/emb.reason: Same pre-widening as app/ above; base/ is the ADR-0562 shared floor and an embedded asset there must be BUCK-srcs-mapped like any other. Created by the first libs/ consolidation move.

Same pre-widening as app/ above; the policy capability (ADR-0615, extracted from iam) will embed Cedar/policy assets, exactly the include_str! class this gate maps. Created when the policy capability lands its first crate.

ci/facade/endpoint-authorization-coverag.reason: Same pre-widening as app/ above. A shared-floor primitive can expose an HTTP control plane; new-surface detection must cover base/ before it holds code.

Same pre-widening as app/ above. The policy capability (ADR-0615, extracted from iam) will expose policy-decision endpoints; an unauthenticated control plane there is the worst case this gate exists to block.

ci/facade/module-membership/capability-m.reason: ADR-0562 capability-first destination for the shared floor. Declared ahead of creation for the same reason as app/; created by the first libs/ consolidation move.

Declared capability in the ADR-0562 closed registry with no directory yet; created when the policy-pack capability lands its first crate. This membership `scan_roots` forward declaration is SOUND and stays: scan_roots is pure coverage, so naming a not-yet-existing root costs nothing and the root is walked the moment it appears. Its tier-policy twin (`crate_root_globs::policy/*/*`) was RETIRED 2026-08-01 because the tier policy gives no such free ride: every crate_root_globs root must also appear in service_roots/capability_roots/unclassified_roots (pinned by every_governed_glob_root_is_declared_in_the_policy), and for a crate-less `policy` the only reachable option was `unclassified_roots`, a live SKIP-ALL-EDGES exemption that R6b correctly REDs. The forward declaration therefore structurally required a standing violation to exist, which is why it was baselined rather than fixed. Re-add the glob together with a real root declaration in the same change that lands policy/'s first crate — the ADR-0615 re-home of the nine iam-mapped Cedar/PDP crates, filed separately as a MOVE.

_dark_gate_comment: FROZEN shrink-only baseline of gate crates whose entire test suite runs on fixtures and therefore evaluates nothing about this repository. Grandfathered so the check could land without first rewriting every entry -- refusing to run until the corpus is clean is exactly what kept this blind spot open. A crate that gains a live-corpus test must be REMOVED here in the same change (stale_dark_gate_baseline fires otherwise), so the burn-down is recorded and cannot silently reverse. Nothing may be ADDED: a new gate crate must ship a live-corpus test.

exempt_gate_crates.planning-projection: Not a gate. ci/facade/planning-projection is a pure projection library: it declares no gate id and no violation codes, exposes no check() entry, and its own header states it 'deliberately accepts an already-derived masterplan projection... keeping filesystem/process concerns at the edge'. The generated-artifact controller materializes its input and drives it. Demanding a live-corpus test of a library that takes no filesystem input would be noise. The ci/facade/ prefix is a cheap universe, not a definition of gate-ness.
